rachel (devex): Quick note from a user session: sampleapp used my org token instead of the project token and it silently succeeded. super confusing for new users.

omar (sdk): yikes. did they set both envs?

rachel (devex): yes: had REDWOOD_ORG_TOKEN in shell and followed quickstart that sets REDWOOD_PROJECT_TOKEN. container helper returns keyring token first.

lia (platform): loader precedence bug then. current helper does keyring -> env -> metadata. should be env -> keyring -> metadata.

omar (sdk): i'll flip the order and add tests for all combos. also change keyring API to store namespaced keys `redwood:project:<id>` and `redwood:org:<id>` so cached tokens can't clobber each other.

chuck (security): namespacing + audit logs for write ops please. and require interactive confirmation when rotating org-scoped keys locally.

rachel (devex): UX: can we log a one-line startup warning when both org and project envs are present: "Both REDWOOD_ORG_TOKEN and REDWOOD_PROJECT_TOKEN set; using REDWOOD_PROJECT_TOKEN" with link to docs.

omar (sdk): makes sense. also adding a metric for "env-conflict" so we can monitor how often this trips people.

lia (platform): devops ask: add a CI/Dockerfile lint to fail builds that reference org-scoped envs so images don't bake org tokens.

ci-bot: issue #631 opened: Dockerfile/CI scan for REDWOOD_ORG_TOKEN usage. Assigned to lia.

omar (sdk): PR: https://git.redwood/sdks/patch/flip-loader-99 flips precedence, adds keyring namespacing, and unit tests. Left TODO for audit logs and confirm on rotate.

chuck (security): once PR merges, add migration doc and a tiny tool to migrate legacy unscoped keyring entries to namespaced entries.

rachel (devex): thanks team. i'll update the quickstart guide to show the warning and explicitly unset org env in the Dockerfile so new users don't hit this. closing after PR + docs + lint. :thumbsup:
